title: Karnataka Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti Resigns After 46-Year Legislative Career
excerpt: The 80-year-old BJP leader and eight-time MLC steps down as Chairman of the Karnataka Legislative Council, ending one of Indian politics' longest legislative tenures.
body:
• Basavaraj Horatti, 80, has resigned as Chairman of the Karnataka Legislative Council on August 7, 2026, ending a tenure that began in December 2022
  • Horatti has served as an MLC since 1980, winning eight consecutive terms from the Karnataka West Teachers' constituency — one of the longest legislative tenures in Indian history
  • The resignation comes amid a long-running political tug-of-war with the ruling Congress government, which had been seeking to install its own candidate in the chair

Horatti Steps Down After Decades in Office

Basavaraj Horatti, the longest-serving member of the Karnataka Legislative Council, has resigned as its Chairman, bringing to a close a tenure marked by political turbulence and cross-party respect. The 80-year-old BJP leader stepped down on August 7, 2026, according to updates on the Karnataka Legislature records and confirmed by multiple reports.

Horatti had been serving as Chairman since December 21, 2022, his third stint in the role. He previously held the chairmanship from June to December 2018 and again from February 2021 to May 2022, when he resigned to join the BJP from the Janata Dal (Secular).

"In 42 years of my political life, this is my first change. I first got elected as an independent and thereafter got associated with the then Janata Dal and its breakaway JD(S)."

— Basavaraj Horatti, in 2022 upon joining BJP

A Political Career Spanning Five Decades

Born on April 14, 1946, in Alagundi, Horatti first won election to the Karnataka Legislative Council in 1980 from the Karnataka West Teachers' constituency. He went on to win eight consecutive terms, making him one of the longest-serving legislators in the country's history, according to The Hindu.

Over his career, Horatti served as Minister of Primary and Secondary Education under Chief Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy (2006–2007), Minister of Law and Parliamentary Affairs (2006), and Minister of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj under Chief Minister Dharam Singh (2004–2006). He was widely regarded as a prominent Lingayat face of north Karnataka politics.

Congress Pressure Behind the Exit

The resignation follows months of political maneuvering by the ruling Congress party, which controls the Karnataka state government. According to a report by The Hindu in late 2025, Congress had been seeking to unseat Horatti but lacked the numbers in the Legislative Council to force a change. The party was expected to wait until 2026 council elections, when 16 seats were set to become vacant, to secure a clearer majority.

Horatti had maintained his position as Chairman despite belonging to the opposition BJP, a rare arrangement in Indian state politics. Political analysts noted that his cross-party stature and seniority had made any overt move against him politically costly for Congress, according to FirstPiper.

What the Resignation Means for Karnataka

With both the Chairman and Deputy Chairman posts now vacant — the Deputy Chairman position held by M.K. Pranesh had already been lying unfilled — the state cabinet will need to appoint a pro-tem Chairman and seek the Governor's approval. The Congress government is expected to move quickly to install its own nominee.

The Legislative Council, known as the Vidhan Parishad, is the upper house of Karnataka's bicameral legislature and plays a key role in reviewing and passing legislation. The process to elect a new Chairman is expected to begin in the coming weeks.

Diaspora Context

For Indian Americans tracking politics in their home states, Horatti's departure marks the end of an era in Karnataka — a state with a significant diaspora population in the United States, particularly in technology hubs like the Bay Area and Seattle.

What's Next

The Congress government is now expected to push for a Chairman from its own ranks, which would give it greater control over the upper house's legislative agenda. How the BJP responds, and whether Horatti takes on a new role within the party, remains to be seen.
